guide.title: Anchorage Golf Course: Golf in Anchorage, Alaska
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State list ranks Anchorage Golf Course first in Alaska — a list of only two courses, which Golf Digest itself describes as "an abbreviated Best in State list based on just a dozen or so evaluations from some ambitious travelers," adding, "It's also not simple to get panelists there." Anchorage Golf Course carries Golf Digest's own "Public" label and sits at 3651 O'Malley Road, Anchorage, AK 99507, a Municipality of Anchorage Public Facility. Alaska has no counties: the state legislature's own research service records that the Organic Act of 1912 barred a county government here, and the jurisdiction that administers this address names itself, in its own 2024 financial report, the Municipality of Anchorage. Bill Newcomb designed the course, which opened in 1987; Forrest Richardson, ASGCA, began a renovation in 2008 that his own project page expects to conclude in 2028. The course states its golf season runs from early May through mid-October. Moose Run Golf Course's Creek Course, second on the same two-entry list and also labelled "Public," is this guide's day-two course.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: Ted Stevens Anchorage International Airport (ANC) is the gateway. The golf course's own directions page states: "From the airport drive east on International Airport Road for approximately 1.5 miles to Minnesota Boulevard. Turn right (south) on Minnesota. Follow Minnesota (south and then east following the curve in the road) until you reach the New Seward Highway. Minnesota becomes O'Malley Road at this point. Follow this road for approximately 2 miles until you reach the Anchorage Golf Course sign on the left hand side of the road." From downtown Anchorage, the same page gives a second route: "Start by heading west on 5th Avenue. Make a left (south) on L Street. Drive down L Street going past Westchester Lagoon. L Street becomes Minnesota Drive. Continue driving for approximately six miles. Minnesota Drive becomes O'Malley Road at this point. Follow this road for approximately 2 miles until you reach the Anchorage Golf Course sign on the left hand side of the road." The address is 3651 O'Malley Road, Anchorage, AK 99507. Moose Run Golf Course, the day-two course, operates at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, but its two courses sit outside the base gates: civilians reach it from the Glenn Highway at the Arctic Valley Road exit without passing a base checkpoint.

sections.heading: Anchorage Golf Course
sections.body: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State list ranks Anchorage Golf Course first in Alaska, carrying its own "Public" label; the course's Golf Digest profile records the same result before, in 1989, 2017-'20 and 2025-'26. But the list itself holds only two courses, and Golf Digest says so in its own words: "It's also not simple to get panelists there, thus an abbreviated Best in State list based on just a dozen or so evaluations from some ambitious travelers." Bill Newcomb designed and built the original course, which opened in 1987; the operator's own course page credits him as "renowned golf course architect Bill Newcomb." Forrest Richardson, ASGCA, began a renovation in 2008 that his own project page describes as done a few holes at a time, "due to Alaska's short growing season," with work expected to conclude in 2028. The course hosted a USGA championship in 2022. The operator describes the course as a "6,600 yard test"; Golf Digest's own course profile lists it at 6,601 yards, slope rating 129, with 32 bunkers. The course states its golf season runs from early May through mid-October, with the golf shop open year-round. In midsummer, the operator notes play can run from as early as 5 a.m. to after midnight.

sections.heading: Playing it
sections.body: Tee times are open to anyone; there is no membership, residency or affiliation requirement. The standard booking window is five days in advance. Out-of-state visitors are an explicit exception: the course invites travellers to request a tee time ahead of that five-day policy through a form on its Out of State page, and staff then confirm the booking. Single players cannot reserve online and are handled as walk-ons or on the stand-by list. At least 24 hours notice must be given to cancel or make changes to a tee time; online booking requires a valid credit card, and tee times can also be booked by phone at (907) 522-3363. The course's 2026 Rates & Fees page lists 18 holes at $84.00 Non Resident, $57.50 Alaska Resident, $55.00 Senior Resident and $17.00 Junior; 9 holes at $55.00, $37.50, $36.50 and $11.50 respectively; and Twilight at $65.00, $47.00, $44.00 and $17.00. Seniors are defined as 60 and over, Juniors as 17 and under.

sections.heading: At the course
sections.body: O'Malley's on the Green is the bar-and-grill dining room at Anchorage Golf Course. The operator describes it as "Conveniently located just off O'Malley Road at the Anchorage Golf Course," serving "a relaxed atmosphere with a great bar & grill style menu featuring appetizers, salads, fresh cuisine and specialty cocktails." Listed hours: Monday through Saturday, 11:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Sunday, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., with Sunday brunch from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. The operator's page does not say whether these hours hold once the golf season ends in mid-October.

sections.heading: Day two: Moose Run Golf Course (Creek)
sections.body: Moose Run Golf Course's Creek Course sits second on the same Golf Digest Alaska Best in State list, also labelled "Public." The operator's own homepage carries the heading "Creek & Hill Courses Located Outside the Gates of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson." Moose Run is a military golf facility operated at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, but its two courses sit outside the base gates and it is open to the public: the operator states it serves "all Active Duty and Retired Military, Veterans, DoD Employees, their families, and our Civilian Guests," and JBER's own Force Support site confirms the courses "are open to the civilian community." Civilians reach it from the Glenn Highway at the Arctic Valley Road exit without passing a base checkpoint. The Hill Course was established in 1952 by Army Combat Engineers; the Creek Course — the one Golf Digest ranks — opened in 2000, designed by architect Robin Nelson. The course's own rate sheet, updated 08/31/2026, lists civilian Daily Rates of $53 (18 holes) and $36 (9 holes) Monday through Thursday, with a Senior 60+ rate of $50 and $35; and $56 (18 holes) and $39 (9 holes) Friday through Sunday, with a Senior 60+ rate of $53 and $38. Military and DoD tiers are priced separately and lower.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Anchorage Golf Course?
faq.answer: Tee times are open to anyone; there is no membership, residency or affiliation requirement. The standard booking window is five days in advance, online with a valid credit card or by phone at (907) 522-3363. Out-of-state visitors get an explicit exception: the course invites travellers to request a tee time ahead of that five-day policy through a form on its Out of State page, and staff then confirm the booking. Single players cannot reserve online and are handled as walk-ons or on the stand-by list.

faq.question: When is the golf season in Anchorage?
faq.answer: The course states its golf season runs from early May through mid-October, with the golf shop open year-round. In midsummer, the operator notes play can run from as early as 5 a.m. to after midnight.

faq.question: Is Anchorage Golf Course really Alaska's best course?
faq.answer: Golf Digest ranks it first in its 2025-'26 Best in State list for Alaska, but the list holds only two courses, and Golf Digest calls it, in its own words, "an abbreviated Best in State list based on just a dozen or so evaluations from some ambitious travelers," adding, "It's also not simple to get panelists there."

faq.question: Why does this guide say "Municipality of Anchorage" instead of a county?
faq.answer: Alaska has no counties. The state legislature's own research service states the Organic Act of 1912 barred a county government in the territory, and the jurisdiction that administers this address names itself, in its own 2024 financial report, the Municipality of Anchorage — formed in 1975 when the City of Anchorage unified with the Greater Anchorage Area Borough.

faq.question: Do I need base access to play Moose Run?
faq.answer: No. The operator's own homepage heading reads "Creek & Hill Courses Located Outside the Gates of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson," and civilians reach it from the Glenn Highway at the Arctic Valley Road exit without passing a base checkpoint. The operator states the course serves "all Active Duty and Retired Military, Veterans, DoD Employees, their families, and our Civilian Guests," and JBER's own Force Support site confirms the courses "are open to the civilian community."
